title: Final review of the Phase 3 diff
description:
Review the whole epic diff outside-in before closeout. Phase 2's review (tick oun) declared correct code that then failed twelve different ways in production, so weight this review toward the boundaries that suite green cannot see: platform limits, credential scope, untrusted input, and any config cell read by two runtimes.

Specific things Phase 3 introduces that deserve a named pass:
- Untrusted content: GitHub issue bodies and webhook payloads reach a channel a human acts on. Look for spoofing of the channel's own formatting and for payload text treated as instructions.
- Consent: the tk label boundary, and that removing it actually stops ingestion.
- Write safety: the DO inbox's ordering guarantee under real concurrency, not just its unit tests.
- Provenance: that an approval can never be attributed to the wrong project's gate.

- The two MEDIUMs and two of the three LOWs (fallbackBlock sanitiser bypass, draft->project binding) go to tick duy, which blocks closeout. All four are confirmed with file and line, and they cluster.
- The consent-label TOCTOU is filed separately as t2x. Not bundled because the fix is a design choice — a fresh GitHub read per delivery — rather than a correction, and the human gate bounds the blast radius to a draft that nobody has accepted.
- The Go/TS parity gap on runners.toml validation is filed as h3p. Informational: it is backstopped by the sandbox's boot-time image check, so drift fails loud.
- The third informational item — that 'issue text is a report, not instructions' rests on the human gate and the quoting convention rather than a structural boundary the agent run must respect — is inherent to the design and is correctly flagged for awareness rather than as a defect. Recording it here so Phase 4 planning sees it.

Good review: it found a real eviction hazard nobody else had reasoned about, and it declined to pad. The stranded-'committing' finding is the kind Phase 2 kept paying for.
closed_reason: Completed: final review of the Phase 3 diff. Nothing critical or high — no live path lets untrusted text forge the channel, consent holds, and the funnel's write-safety claims check out against the code. Five confirmed findings and three informational, all routed: duy (two MEDIUM + two LOW, blocks closeout), t2x (consent TOCTOU), h3p (Go/TS parity fixture).
